beats.text: To recap. On an energy profile, every quantity is a vertical difference: forward activation energy, reverse activation energy and delta H. A catalyst lowers the peak but leaves both endpoints, and delta H, unchanged. In a thermochemical equation, delta H scales with the coefficients and changes sign when the equation is reversed, and it depends on the states.
Closing recall. An equation has delta H equal to negative one hundred kilojoules. What is delta H for the reverse equation with every coefficient tripled?
Reverse it: positive one hundred. Triple it: positive three hundred kilojoules. Next episode, we step back from equations to the fuels themselves: fossil fuels, biofuels and the carbon cycle.
